failure_modes.name: Query_Form_Mismatch
failure_modes.evidence: Hop 2 query: 'Who is the author of "The Polish Officer" (1995) and what genre is this author famous for? Is this author known primarily for writing historical spy novels?' and Hop 3 query: 'Who is the author of "The Polish Officer" (1995), and is this author primarily known for writing historical spy novels? Is H. P. Lovecraft known for writing historical spy novels?' Both queries are formulated as natural-language yes/no questions bundling multiple targets rather than as focused entity-based retrieval queries.

failure_modes.name: Query_Stagnation
failure_modes.evidence: Hop 2 query asks 'Who is the author of "The Polish Officer" (1995) and what genre is this author famous for? Is this author known primarily for writing historical spy novels?' Hop 3 query repeats nearly identically: 'Who is the author of "The Polish Officer" (1995), and is this author primarily known for writing historical spy novels? Is H. P. Lovecraft known for writing historical spy novels?' The core request about The Polish Officer's authorship and historical spy novel connection is unchanged across hops.

failure_modes.name: Insufficient_Retrieved_Evidence
failure_modes.evidence: Summary 1 explicitly names the missing entity: 'Identification of the author of "The Polish Officer" (1995)' and 'Verification that this identified author is indeed famous for writing historical spy novels'. Hop 2 query targets this: 'Who is the author of "The Polish Officer" (1995) and what genre is this author famous for?' Despite this well-formed targeting, none of the retrieved passages across all three hops mention "The Polish Officer" (1995) or its author.

failure_modes.name: Missing_Evidence_Not_Specified
failure_modes.evidence: Summary 2 states: 'The claim cannot be verified from the provided passages. The passages do not contain any information about H. P. Lovecraft, do not identify the author of "The Polish Officer" (1995)...' However, this summary fails to explicitly name H. P. Lovecraft or The Polish Officer as specific missing entities requiring retrieval focus, unlike Summary 1 which did specify these gaps.

failure_modes.name: Solver_Irrelevant_Passage_Overprocessing
failure_modes.evidence: In hop 1 reasoning, the solver processes seven irrelevant passages one by one: 'Passage [1]: Henry Kitchell Webster - wrote mystery, family drama, science fiction; no mention... Passage [2]: R.L. Stine - horror/children's fiction writer; not about spy novels... Passage [3]: Jack Woodford - pulp novels... Passage [4]: Knut Hamsun - Norwegian author; unrelated...' None of these passages contain relevant information about The Polish Officer or H. P. Lovecraft, yet each receives enumerated analysis.
